      HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET
      ----------------------
Letters are accepted in any form
for publication in OUTLETTERS:
BASIC PRINT or DATA; handwritten
or typed copy; all wordprocessor
files (please state which!) or a
simple JOTTER program is in our
Issue 2(Disk #4).The easiest for
us to edit are Tasword 2 files
with the right margin set at 32.

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From:Ken Bates, KENT



Dear Brian and Ron,

Is my Speccy possessed? I have
just switched on to write this
to you and instead of the usual
opening logo and selection menu
the screen read:-

      HELLO THERE, I'M A +3

What is going on? The machine
was, to all purposes, dead. No
keys would work and the snapshot
button on my Multiface +3 was
also down. Could it be because I
just recently hired'POLTERGEIST'
from the local video store?

Anyway, the point of this letter
was to tell you of something I
did recently that I have never
done before (steady on). I went
to a computer auction. As I have
never been to any kind of
auction before I was a bit wary
in case I sneezed and bought a
Compaq PC for several thousand
mortgage repayments.

The auction was held in a school
in Swanley,Kent and all kinds of
equipment were on offer ranging
from disk boxes to full computer
systems; from "Sold as seen" to
"new and guaranteed". It mostly
catered for the PC world and
unfortunately I saw no Speccy
stuff at all. There was one very
sorry-looking Commodore 64 which
was looked down on by all.

I could only stay for about 45
minutes when the bidding started
(after all, it was FA Cup Final
Day)but in that short time I saw
PC spreadsheet software sold for
two and three pounds and Filofax
wristwatches with PC interfaces
for `24. A 2nd-hand PC with hard
disk sold for `100 or so.


Before the bidding started there
was plenty of opportunity to in-
spect and test the equipment on
display. As the only instruction
I know to use on the PC is DIR
or DIR/P (this gives a catalogue
of files on disk) this is what I
tried).

Anyway, as a cheap entry to the
world of PC computing, I think
this an ideal way to start but I
would suggest either taking
someone with you who knows what
is a good buy or be prepared to
take a chance on a purchase and
maybe a repair or two in the
future.If anyone was thinking of
buying equipment at an auction I
would also take, if possible, a
program on disk to try with the
machines displayed but make sure
the disk is labelled as your own
to avoid any unpleasantness that
may arise.

I fully intend to go to the next
auction in my area and, who
knows, maybe even buy a thing or
two (one 3" disk please and can
I have a receipt?). - Ken Bates

To Ken Bates from Brian

Thanks, Ken.

As far as the strange +3 message
you saw,either there's a special
mode, like the test mode, which
you accidentally triggered by
pressing certain keys or, more
likely, a computer virus was
stored in the extra RAM of your
Multiface 3. If so,check all the
various programs that have come
your way recently to see which
one put it there.

If it occurs again try all your
programs over a period to see if
you can eliminate any it CAN'T
be. I'd be interested to hear if
you track it down!
                       - Brian

From Lee Jon Powis, BIRMINGHAM


Dear Eds,

A few SAM points...

I think it's a great pity that
disk file-handling hasn't been
supported in SAM BASIC.

I've seen a few SAM screens in
the mags of Bugs Bunny, a dragon
and a digitised one of Sigourney
Weaver. I wish they were on my
DOS disk! Has anyone else got
those screens? Also, the other
close-up Tutankamen pic I've
seen in Popular Computing Weekly
is better than the one on the
DOS disk.

My DOS (v1.3) doesn't support ST
disks - I've tried my friends
Degas Elite pics recorded in
standard and 880K format but
with no results. Perhaps the new
DOS will have this promised
feature?


If MGT have already started des-
patch of the new ROMS does this
mean the errors which you've
recently elucidated will be
ignored?

What does BAND do in Sam BASIC?

I would much prefer the keys to
be softer like on my +3 or a PC.
48K+ keyboard or what?

Why is my power pack noisy?My +3
power pack doesn't make a sound.
The shop where I bought the SAM
said it was normal and that they
have none on show because of the
noise. Is your power pack noisy?
I also have a loose screw in the
power pack as did another Coupe
owner I read about.

           L.J. Powis

To Lee Jon Powis from Brian


By "disk-file handling" I assume
you mean handling "open-type" or
"PRINT"files because all regular
types ARE supported.SAM BASIC is
so flexible that if the SAM does
continue to be supported in even
a modest degree then you can be
sure that if MGT (or their
successors) do not produce a new
DOS version to handle PRINT
files then a third-party will do
it somehow.

Both the Bugs Bunny and dragon
screens are in this issue of
OUTLET(with others)in DEMOPIX. I
have the Sigourney Weaver one
and promise to either switch it

for one in this DEMOPIX or put
it on next month with some other
screens we have. I do not know
the Tutankamen screen you
mentioned but it may be either
part of the same one enlarged (I
doubt it as I think you would
know) or it may be the Amiga one
which is much better - looks
more sort of gold-ish and shiny
right? I expect someone will
port it over.


Which brings me to ST disks. I
don't think MGT promised that
the SAM DOS would support ST
disks as such but that a program
would be made available that
could load and convert ST
screens to SAM format. I'd very

much like to get hold of such a
program myself. It must already
exist in prototype form surely
since ST screens have already
been converted? The most I have
done is to read in the sectors
off an ST disc of mine. I could
read the values written to the
sector but I haven't got all my
ST notes and info here now as I
lent the whole lot, machine and
all, to my sister and I can't
just recollect details of how
the Degas and Neochrome screens
are stored on disc let alone how
files are stored. If anyone gets
anywhere with this please let me
know as I would gladly start
buying up some ST PD screens for
inclusion in OUTLET if I had a
convertor.

When I wrote the last lot of SAM
errors I listed in OUTLET 33 I
heard the new ROM and DOS were
soon to be issued and so were
definitely at the end of testing
etc. so I didn't even send MGT
my last list as I knew it must
be too late and anyway, MGT do
subscribe to OUTLET so they can
read about the errors there!

When I first got a SAM I thought
(and still think) the keys were
better than I'd hoped for on a
budget computer.I'm still fairly
satisfied but seem to detect a
slight hard resistance right at
the very start of the press
of some of the keys which is not
very good for touch typing with
the little fingers!

BAND is a BINARY AND and BOR is
a BINARY OR.As you probably know
the ordinary BASIC AND and OR in
Boolean Algebra does not provide
the same function as AND and OR
in machine code. BAND and BOR do
the same as the machine code AND
and OR, that is, BAND takes the
binary value of two values and
creates a new value where each
bit is set if both the bit in
the first value is set AND the
bit in the second value whereas
BOR sets the new bit if either
the first value bit is set OR
the second. Wot - No BXOR?

My power pack hums. Sometimes it
buzzes so I kick it to show it
who's boss and it goes back to a
steady hum. Wouldn't you?

Thanks for the great screens and
the bouncy ball demo which will
go in OUTLET soon if not this
very issue!
                     - Brian

From Ton Voon

Dear Ron,

I recently[end May,early June?]
contacted MGT and on the subject
of Outlet and their neglect, I
received the following reply...

"...that OUTLET are now on our
Press List and will receive all
the latest news on the COUPE."

Do you buy that?Keep the readers
posted, please.

Concerning the new SAM version
of OUTLET with its larger memory
and disk capacity; are you going
to have more structured
programs? Currently, I'm having

pretty tough problems decipher-
ing how your programs are
working.Maybe you could have the
full, unextended program on disk
to be compressed by readers or
vice-versa if enough information
is shown how it works. What do
other readers think?

Having corresponded with Tasman
earlier,they have taken the time
to send me a letter about their
release of Tasword 2 for the SAM
Coupe. It says, and I quote:


"Tasword 2 is the same as on the
48K Spectrum except that some
keypresses have been changed to
reflect the different keyboard."

Considering the large acclaim
for T2 on the Spectrum, I am
hoping to purchase it. I only
hope there will be more of an
upgrade later. By the way, it
costs `19.95 for disc or tape,
but the tape version isn't ready
until the middle of May.

Thank you for Outlet 26.SUPERMAT
is indeed an extraordinary
program. I also read with great
interest the editorial - since
subscriptions are easier for you
to process (and for my conveni-
ence), I'll start from the next
issue but I've a few questions:
Do I still have to return the
Outlet wallet? It's not that I
don't want to; on the contrary,
it encourages communication;it's
just that it is time consuming.

Also what happened to the
envelopes? Are there no more?
Plus I didn't get an order form
or is this under modification?

How do you unhide and unprotect
files on the SAM?

Thanks for listening. Continue
the great work.

            Ton Voon

To Ton Voon from Brian


I have no policy or plans for
more-structured programs in
OUTLET. For me,program structure
is not an end in itself but just
one of many things to consider
when writing a program such as
speed of writing the program;
the running speed of the program
(not the same thing); economy of
memory and storage space;
compatibility with other program
modules common to all or many
OUTLET programs etc.Furthermore,
as I have stated in an early
OUTLET article; DO-LOOPS,EXIT IF
and DEF PROCS etc. do not add to
the structure of a program at
all! Consider the following...

1000 REM START
 ...program
1100 GOTO 1000

    ...which is EXACTLY the same
program structure as...

1000 DO
 ...program
1100 LOOP

Both of the above routines are
structured to carry out the
instructions between 1000 and
1100 and jump back to 1000. Both
do EXACTLY the same and the only
difference is in the words used.
The advantage of using DO LOOP
is the convenience of not having
to remember or look at what line
number to GO TO.

I am a great fan of procedures
which are PERFECTLY implemented
in SAM BASIC and will be using
them extensively. However they
are simply a neater and better
way of performing a GO SUB which
is EXACTLY WHAT THEY ARE.

SHOWMENU is exactly the same
structure as GO SUB SHOWMENU (as
a variable) or GO SUB 9000 or
CALL 65000 in machine code. They
all do the same structurally
which is to USE a subroutine and
then continue from where the
program left off.

Now,add to all that lot the fact
that most OUTLET programs are
not written by me anyway but by
many different readers with a
wide variety of programming

skills and views on structure
and you can see that the short
answer to your question is "no".

Common to most OUTLET programs
are....
  10
 TO   AUTHOR'S BASIC
7900
8000  OUTLET LINK BASIC,INTRO
 TO   AND TITLE PAGE ETC...
8900
9000  OUTLET OR AUTHOR'S SUB-
 TO   ROUTINES (E.G. PRINTOUT/
9899  SAVE/LOAD OPTIONS
9900  CODE IN REMS
9970
 TO   PROGRAM SAVE ROUTINES
9985
9986
 TO   CODE IN REMS
9999

The program start line will
often be 8000 to display the
title page and intro. Pressing
"R" will usually RUN the program
from line 1 and a "Q" to quit
will usually return to 8000 and
so to exit the program by
selecting NEXT ITEM etc.


Sorry there's no easy answer but
I'm always willing to help
clarify individual program parts
if I can.If it's any consolation
then be assured that I, myself,
don't understand some programs
that get contributed!

If you liked SUPERMAT then you
will be delighted with HIFORM in
this issue!

No,the OUTLET wallet need not be
returned by subscribers where
CHEZRON provide the media.If you
have one then retain it and use
it to send letters,contributions
etc. Ron usually returns it with
another window envelope for you
to use.

I've passed Ron a note to check
you get an order form/envelope
if that has not already been
done.

You "UNHIDE" Sam files with HIDE
OFF "FILENAME"and you"UNPROTECT"
using PROTECT OFF "FILENAME" but
it's easier to use Brian Gaff's
excellent AUTOmenu in Issue 34.

                       - Brian

From M.E. Tomlin,  MABLETHORPE

Dear Brian/Ron,

My set up comprises a +3 and
Citizen 120D printer and I would
like to print out some of the
items but can only do this using
a Multiface 3. With the 120D it
is necessary to POKE 23354,62
and 23355,16 before the +3 will
talk to it in addition to the
FORMAT LPRINT "U" instruction.
I have tried POKEing these in
(using the Multiface)but without
success. I had hoped TABLOID
might work but no joy. When I
select 3 from the print menu,
everything just locks up! Can
you advise?
              - M.E. Tomlin

To Mr. M.E. Tomlin from Brian

I believe those POKEs were
recommended to solve a fault on
the +3 which, presumably, was
cured on later +3's because I do
not have to use the POKEs and
all OUTLET print routines work
perfectly on my +3. Try this...

Select +3 BASIC and enter MERGE
"CONTENTS" then LIST 1420 and
add the POKEs at the start of
line 1420 before the FORMAT.Then
press ENTER to re-enter the line
and enter RUN. Try the printout
from any OUTLET text file but if
it still does not work put the
POKEs AFTER the FORMAT in 1420.
Has anyone else any suggestions?

                        - Brian

From J. Hunter,  NORTHAMPTON

I was an early purchasers of the
SAM COUPE with just one drive
and 512K RAM. I have followed
with interest all the comments
you and various readers have
made concerning the COUPE. I am
still awaiting [12.6.90] the ROM
and DOS update (I have DOS 1.1).

The main reason I am writing to
you is to let you know I have
purchased the disk version of
Tasword 2 for the SAM. This
letter is written using it.
[N.B. a disc with the text file
on it would be much appreciated
on future letters to save me
typing it all in again. - all
discs returned! - B.C.]

I know it is only the Spectrum
version adapted for SAM and
later this year TASMAN will be
issuing a true SAM version. The
only problem I am experiencing
is that the key depression
response is ultra-sensitive in
that I get qute a lot of repeat
letters - I assure you I don't
leave my fingers on the key(s)
any longer than necessary. Can a
POKE or POKEs be entered in the
BASIC to make key depression
less critical?

A final question... I would like
to change over to receiving the
SAM disc version of OUTLET but
would it be best to wait until
MGT supply me with updated ROM
and DOS?             J. Hunter.

To Mr. J. Hunter from Brian

Yes, you can add the following
POKEs to the TASWORD BASIC (top
line) to change key response...

  POKE 23561,35 : POKE 23562,5

23561 holds the value for the
delay before the key STARTS to
repeat and 23562 holds the value
for the delay between successive
repeats.The POKEs work on SAM or
Spectrum and the above values
are the default values for the
Spectrum (SAM = 33 and 3).If you
increase the 35 to 40 or 50 and
the 5 to say, 10 it will SLOW
key response. If you search the
TASWORD BASIC you will probably
see one or both POKEs with LOWER

values and that's the cause of
the extra sensitivity. You could
remove any such POKEs you find
if you wish but it doesn't
matter so long as YOUR POKEs are
in the line just before the text
editor is called (normally a
USR command in the top line).

If the above fails to work write
again and, if possible, send a
copy of the BASIC listing as it
is possible the program flow may
be different on the version you
have.

If you switch to SAM now you may
have problems with one or two of
the programs but I somehow don't
think it will be long before you
get your new ROM...
                       - Brian

From Stephen D. Watson

In the last few months I've been
having problems loading from my
3.5" drive ( I have a 128K+
connected to a Plus D(G+DOS1)via
a RAM turbo joystick interface).
The following error messages are
fairly frequent - "FORMAT DATA
LOST", "FILE NOT FOUND" and "NO
SYS+FILE".Regular drive cleaning
has caused no improvement.

My usual methods of overcoming
this are to re-boot the system
(which generally fails) or re-
boot with my original system
disc and loading a file recovery
program(FORMAT VOL.1; No.6; P.9)
and recovering any file. This
allows me to CAT the disc and
load any program.

More recently, I have found a
routine, written to step heads
over a cleaning disc (FORMAT VOL
3; No.3; P.16), when run, gives
immediate access to catalogue
and programs on a disc.

My system is not heavily used -
not enough to make worn heads a
possibility - and while my
solutions allow me to use the
system,it can be frustrating and
time-consuming. Any help you can
give would be most welcome.

May I also take this opportunity
to congratulate you on a well-
produced and entertaining magaz-
ine. While I am only a "semi-
serious" user, I have found many
of the articles extremly useful.
           - Stephen D. Watson

To Stephen Watson from Brian

Thanks,Stephen.There are several
things that may be causing the
problem. First, what brand of
disc are you using? If mixed,try
to check if one certain type
give the most problem. You might
try a different brand or source
as we have certainly found some
discs give more errors than
others.

You could try removing the RAM
Turbo joystick for a while. This
is just a guess but it may be
interfering with the +D in some
way.

I have no details of the differ-
ences between the various

versions of +D DOS. Can anyone
else please write in if they can
clarify or offer any suggestions
because I do not have access to
a +D. It may be there is a later
version of the DOS which will
cure the problem.

The problem could be a drive or
+D hardware fault of course but
my feeling is that it is either
a fault in GDOS 1 or poor discs.

Finally, but most importantly,
ALWAYS keep a back up of EVERY
file of any significance on a
SEPARATE disc. This doubles the
cost of storage but data is so
fragile I never dream of only
having one copy of anything.

                     - Brian

Alan Fortune, 47 Northumberland
Avenue, NUNEATON, Warwickshire,
            CV10 8ER

First off,keep up the good work!
Its great to see somebody keep-
ing the Spectrum scene alive!

I noticed a letter from Trevor
Wright, in a recent issue of
Outlet, which mentioned a
conversion tape for The WRITER
word processor. I've been trying
to get this tape since February,
but I've had no luck. In sheer
frustration I decided to
dissassemble it and modify it
myself. What a task, as it
consists of 18.5K of Code +
another 8K of print-merge Code,
and 8K of installation Code.

However,I've learnt a great deal
about the program and have
developed many modifications
which I find useful. The
typeface can be modified, so
also can the UDGs which I have
redesigned to match the printed
characters they represent. The
Interface One test can be
deleted allowing a Plus D and
two drives to be used instead of
microdrives. I haven't trapped
all the errors yet which can
crash the program occasionally,
but I'm working on it.

My biggest problem is getting
hold of technical details of the
Plus D. Hasn't anyone published
a book on the Plus D?. Finding
details of the error routines is

next to impossible. I also de-
feated the border routine which
now leaves the border black when
you select white paper. I can
supply details of these mods and
many others I haven't listed, to
anyone who cares to write to me
at the above address.

Ernie Taylor wrote you regarding
transferal of Hisoft Basic to a
Plus D system. You must use the
original cassette which includes
a back-up function to tape which
you can break into and change to
SAVE d1 etc. but the program
compiles OK and then hangs when
it should return to BASIC.

If you press BREAK, you are ret-
urned to BASIC, sometimes! Other

times the lot just disappears up
its own output port!. I don't
know how to stop this.Any ideas?

As for Harold Burton's letter
asking how to fit a composite
video lead to his Spectrum;
Assuming it's a standard
Spectrum: Get some coax cable;
solder the centre wire to the
middle lead of the Modulator box
(large silver box in the top
left hand corner of the PCB) and
solder the outer braiding to one
of the small tabs that keep the
modulator lid clipped on. At
work, we simply added a BNC plug
to the other end and plugged it
into our vision mixer. It makes
a very cheap video titler using
Campbell software's DLAN display
language.          - Alan

To Alan Fortune from Brian

Many, many thanks, Alan.

Please note only a printout of
the ARTIST II mods were received
by us.Can you send the mods
themselves? Thanks.I think many
will find the POKEs very useful.
Sorry I don't have time to type
listings in and anyway, I might
introduce an error! You might
also consider writing an article
for OUTLET on the other mods and
+D info you mention? I'm sure it
would be of interest.

Does anyone know if MGT issued
any formal technical information
for the +D?
                         - Brian

From Chris Ingram, MALAWI


Dear Ron & Brian

Short of reformatting (and that
doesn't always work) is there
any way to isolate corrupted
sectors so that they are not
used? Betterbytes Disc Organiser
works quite often, but not every
time. I have several discs with
"junk" files on them which as
soon as they are erased the bad
sector comes up again in a
future save. When a catalogue
sector fails (as in my Outlet
31) there seems to be nothing
one can do: both loading and
saving cause the sector error to
come up. Help!

Is it still possible to obtain
Bonabanner, and if so, how much
is it?

Please congratulate DATON
Software for some unusual and
challenging board games. I have
enjoyed Shanghai in particular,
and even managed to complete it
on my black and white televi-
sion. There does seem to be a
bug in the program as when one
returns to play again after a
failure the board is not
assembled correctly. I inserted
a RUN into the listing and all
seemed to be well.

Kemshu is another one I find
enjoyable to relax with after a
hard day's work, though I have


to look carefully when it's
being set up to find the target
colour (in black & white).

Last week the group of schools
to which I belong held a
Computer In-Service Day and I
was able to promote the idea of
the Spectrum as a serious
machine. I decided to use
Wordmaster/Typeliner/Headliner
instead of a straight word-
processor as I have found it
very useful in my work,
producing test- and work-sheets,
notices, certificates,timetables
and scripts of playlets, for
example. My colleagues at the
other schools were most
impressed with what this suite
of programs can do.

I also set up LOGO with some
worksheets for the teachers to
try. There was an enquiry about
LOGO in a recent Outletter. We
have the version published by
Sinclair Research which we
obtained in the mid-80s. This is
the full implementation of the
language and is well documented.
I don't know if it is still
available.


Can you tell me if the DISCiPLE
is still being produced? I read
somewhere that Datel Electronics
have taken over production of
the +D from MGT to allow them to
concetrate on SAM, but there was
no mention of the DISCiPLE.

It would be a pity to see it
discontinued: we have two at
Hillview School, although I
haven't had much success trying
to network them: whether the
leads or connections are faulty
I don't know, but when the two
are connected they seem to crash
all the time. Loading the Pupil
from the Master is a pain, too:
it takes much longer than
loading the Master and will not
respond to the d* instruction,
it has to be d1. It also throws
up "Nonsense in Basic" if it
meets a POKE @ or CLS # command.

The pupil frequently refuses to
load anything, or needs the
Master resetting before willing
to accept a loading command.

I've given up and gone back to
tape loading. The Master (a

To Ton Voon from Brian

I have no policy or plans for more-structured programs in OUTLET. For me,program structure is not an end in itself but just one of many things to consider when writing a program such as speed of writing the program; the running speed of the program (not the same thing); economy of memory and storage space; compatibility with other program modules common to all or many OUTLET programs etc.Furthermore, as I have stated in an early OUTLET article; DO-LOOPS,EXIT IF and DEF PROCS etc. do not add to the structure of a program at all! Consider the following...

1000 REM START ...program 1100 GOTO 1000

...which is EXACTLY the same program structure as...

1000 DO ...program 1100 LOOP

Both of the above routines are structured to carry out the instructions between 1000 and 1100 and jump back to 1000. Both do EXACTLY the same and the only difference is in the words used. The advantage of using DO LOOP is the convenience of not having to remember or look at what line number to GO TO.

I am a great fan of procedures which are PERFECTLY implemented in SAM BASIC and will be using them extensively. However they are simply a neater and better way of performing a GO SUB which is EXACTLY WHAT THEY ARE.

SHOWMENU is exactly the same structure as GO SUB SHOWMENU (as a variable) or GO SUB 9000 or CALL 65000 in machine code. They all do the same structurally which is to USE a subroutine and then continue from where the program left off.

Now,add to all that lot the fact that most OUTLET programs are not written by me anyway but by many different readers with a wide variety of programming

skills and views on structure and you can see that the short answer to your question is "no".

Common to most OUTLET programs are.... 10 TO   AUTHOR'S BASIC 7900 8000  OUTLET LINK BASIC,INTRO TO   AND TITLE PAGE ETC... 8900 9000  OUTLET OR AUTHOR'S SUB- TO   ROUTINES (E.G. PRINTOUT/ 9899  SAVE/LOAD OPTIONS 9900  CODE IN REMS 9970 TO   PROGRAM SAVE ROUTINES 9985 9986 TO   CODE IN REMS 9999

The program start line will often be 8000 to display the title page and intro. Pressing "R" will usually RUN the program from line 1 and a "Q" to quit will usually return to 8000 and so to exit the program by selecting NEXT ITEM etc.

Sorry there's no easy answer but I'm always willing to help clarify individual program parts if I can.If it's any consolation then be assured that I, myself, don't understand some programs that get contributed!

Yes, you can add the following POKEs to the TASWORD BASIC (top line) to change key response...

POKE 23561,35 : POKE 23562,5

values and that's the cause of the extra sensitivity. You could remove any such POKEs you find if you wish but it doesn't matter so long as YOUR POKEs are in the line just before the text editor is called (normally a USR command in the top line).

### Ответ Ton Voon от Brian

У меня нет никаких правил или планов по поводу «более структурированных» программ в OUTLET. Для меня структура программы — не самоцель, а лишь один из многих факторов, которые нужно учитывать при написании: например, скорость написания программы; скорость её работы (а это не одно и то же); экономия памяти и места на диске; совместимость с другими программными модулями, общими для всех или многих программ OUTLET, и т. д. Более того, как я уже писал в одной из ранних статей OUTLET, всякие DO-LOOP, EXIT IF и DEF PROC вообще не добавляют программе структуры! Посудите сами...

```text
1000 REM START
 ...program
1100 GOTO 1000
```

...это СОВЕРШЕННО та же программная структура, что и...

```text
1000 DO
 ...program
1100 LOOP
```

Обе вышеуказанные процедуры структурированы так, чтобы выполнять команды между строками 1000 и 1100 и прыгать обратно на 1000. Обе делают АБСОЛЮТНО то же самое, и разница лишь в используемых словах. Преимущество использования DO LOOP — в удобстве: не нужно помнить или смотреть, на какой номер строки делать GOTO.

Я большой поклонник процедур, которые ИДЕАЛЬНО реализованы в SAM BASIC, и буду активно их использовать. Однако они являются лишь более аккуратным и удобным способом выполнения GO SUB, ЧЕМ ОНИ, СОБСТВЕННО, И ЯВЛЯЮТСЯ.

SHOWMENU структурно точно такой же, как GO SUB SHOWMENU (через переменную), или GO SUB 9000, или CALL 65000 в машинном коде. Все они делают структурно одно и то же: ИСПОЛЬЗУЮТ подпрограмму, а затем продолжают работу с места вызова.

Теперь добавьте ко всему этому тот факт, что большинство программ в OUTLET написаны вовсе не мной, а множеством разных читателей с самым разным уровнем мастерства программирования и взглядами на структуру, и вы поймете, что краткий ответ на ваш вопрос — «нет».

Общим для большинства программ в OUTLET является следующее:

```text
  10
  ПО   BASIC АВТОРА
7900
8000  СВЯЗУЮЩИЙ BASIC OUTLET, ИНТРО,
  ПО   ТИТУЛЬНАЯ СТРАНИЦА И Т.Д...
8900
9000  ПОДПРОГРАММЫ OUTLET ИЛИ АВТОРА
  ПО   (НАПР. ВЫВОД НА ПЕЧАТЬ /
9899  ОПЦИИ SAVE/LOAD)
9900  КОД В REM-АХ
9970
  ПО   ПРОЦЕДУРЫ СОХРАНЕНИЯ ПРОГРАММЫ
9985
9986
  ПО   КОД В REM-АХ
9999
```

Строкой запуска программы часто является 8000, чтобы показать титульный экран и интро. Нажатие «R» обычно запускает программу (RUN) со строки 1, а «Q» для выхода обычно возвращает на 8000, позволяя выйти из программы выбором NEXT ITEM и т. д.

Да, вы можете добавить следующие POKE в TASWORD BASIC (самая верхняя строка), чтобы изменить отклик клавиатуры...

```text
POKE 23561,35 : POKE 23562,5
```
